analysis_role: Post-result mechanistic falsification of the already-supported transition-regime H1. Test whether environmental tracking is bidirectionally reversible across U->D and D->U transition probabilities, rather than being carried only by one direction.
interpretation: Under the frozen strict nine-taxon CTMC/Brownian estimator, U->D transition probability aligns with the predeclared higher-BIO15/lower-BIO1 niche direction and D->U transition probability aligns with the exact opposite niche direction on all six accepted topologies. The weaker of the two directional alignments is more extreme than 123/126 count-preserving alternative state maps. This supports bidirectional reversible present-niche transition-regime tracking, not historical climate causation or adaptation.
claim_boundary: This is a post-result directional decomposition of H1, not independent confirmation.
Bidirectional alignment shows reversible present-niche transition-regime tracking under the declared estimator, not historical climatic causation or adaptation.
It does not establish that the environment at the actual transition time changed in the inferred direction.
No new environmental axis, taxon, threshold, or mechanism was admitted after result inspection.
